passage:
The corridor was empty after the last bell. Neelam, Kiran's friend since Class 6, found Kiran by the water cooler, staring at the floor.
"You didn't say anything in English class today."
"They laughed when I said 'vater'. Everyone did." Kiran's voice cracked. "I'm never speaking again."
"Who laughed? Arjun?"
"All of them. I came from the village school, Neelam. My English is only..."
"Your maths answers are the best in class. And I say 'sheep' like 'ship'. Sit with me at lunch tomorrow. We'll read the lesson aloud together, and you can practise on me."
Kiran wiped an eye. "Just you?"
"And Meera. She's kind."

qa.q: Where did Neelam find Kiran after the last bell?
qa.a: Neelam found Kiran by the water cooler in the empty corridor.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling after being laughed at over the word "vater"?
qa.a: Kiran felt ashamed and hurt. The cracking voice and the vow of never speaking again show how deeply the laughter stung.

qa.q: What small step did Neelam offer to help Kiran speak again?
qa.a: Neelam invited Kiran to sit together at lunch and read the lesson aloud, so Kiran could practise on a friend. It was a low-pressure start with supportive people.

qa.q: What might Neelam want Kiran to know when Neelam admits saying "sheep" like "ship"?
qa.a: Neelam wants Kiran to know that everyone makes mistakes with English and it does not measure ability. Sharing a mistake makes Kiran feel less alone.

grounding: A teenager from a village school is mocked over an English word, stops speaking in class, and a friend offers supportive practice.

passage:
I am Shankar. My school in Vidarbha taught in Marathi and I learnt English from books. In Class 9 in the city school I read aloud once, and a boy imitated the way I said "world". Half the room laughed.
After that I kept my hand down. Even when I knew the answer I felt my throat tighten, and my face got hot. Teachers marked me "quiet".
Then Simran, who sat next to me, said one day, "I also stumble on 'thorough'. Want to make a reading pair? Ten minutes at lunch." We read paragraph after paragraph. By December I put my hand up, shaking a little, and the room was quiet in the good way.

qa.q: Which subject language had Shankar's earlier school in Vidarbha used?
qa.a: Shankar's school in Vidarbha taught in Marathi.

qa.q: How did Shankar feel after the boy imitated the way Shankar said "world"?
qa.a: Shankar felt ashamed and afraid of being laughed at again. The tight throat and hot face show it, and that is why the hand stayed down.

qa.q: What did Simran do that helped Shankar speak up again?
qa.a: Simran admitted stumbling on "thorough" too and suggested a reading pair at lunch. Practising together in private helped Shankar's confidence grow until a hand went up.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Simran to offer the reading pair?
qa.a: Simran may have felt a little shy but kind, sharing a weakness first so Shankar would not feel alone. It took some courage to admit stumbling too.

grounding: A teenager from a vernacular school is mocked for accent, stops speaking in class, and regains confidence with a supportive peer.
